newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kabila must show political responsibility-Kinkel.
newsitem.headline: Kabila must show political responsibility-Kinkel.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel on Wednesday called on Zaire's new rulers under rebel leader Laurent Kabila to ensure a swift transition to democracy and urged them to show a sense of political responsibility.

Kinkel said he regretted the loss of lives on all sides and called on Kabila, whose forces toppled Zaire's dictator Mobutu Sese Seko at the weekend, to keep a sense of proportion and reiterated Bonn's willingness to cooperate with him.
"We are taking Kabila at his word. The words must follow deeds. Now he is responsible for leading the country to a democratic and peaceful future," Kinkel said in a statement.

Kinkel said Kabila had agreed to observe human rights, form a transitional government, form a legislative body within 60 days, prepare for free elections in the next 12 months and honour the country's existing international obligations.
"In the current transition phase (to democracy) all sides must show reason, a sense of proportion and political responsibility," Kinkel said.
Kinkel said he regretted the deaths of two Frenchmen shot dead in the capital Kinshasha on Tuesday and called for an end to what he called acts of revenge.
On Saturday, Kinkel hailed the end of Mobutu's 32-year rule and said it opened the way for a new, democratic start in Zaire.
